headline: Sainsbury's launched SmartLists in its app, an AI feature that turns a typed or photographed shopping list into real products with Nectar prices.
score_reason: Real consumer launch with little detail on how the AI performs; a UK-specific grocery feature; score kept.
importance_line: Sainsbury's shoppers can build a basket from a typed or photographed list, though the company gives no figures on accuracy and the report relies on its own description.
summary: Decision Marketing reports that Sainsbury's is launching SmartLists in its app, where customers type or photograph a list, such as "ingredients for spaghetti bolognese", and the feature matches it to real products with Nectar Prices that can be added straight to an online trolley. The upgrade also adds an in-store product finder and merges the retailer's online grocery, ChopChop, SmartLists, in-store SmartShop and Nectar services into one app, according to the supermarket.
notes: Retail Week page (chunk link) returned 405; read at Decision Marketing, which carries the Sainsbury's announcement. Sainsbury's own press release exists on corporate.sainsburys.co.uk but was not readable.
